after: t1-diloco FAIL (results/t1/README.md): DiLoCo lost 11 % (H=50) and 29 % (H=250) against DDP at 2,000 steps; H=250 had only 8 outer steps and was unstable.
question: With 2.5x longer training (5,000 steps) and H=100 (50 outer steps), does DiLoCo come within 5 % of DDP while each worker sends at least 100x fewer bytes?
method: As t1-diloco (fabric/pilot.py, same model, data, schedule, 4 workers, new seeds). Outer step: SGD with Nesterov momentum unless an arm says otherwise.

gate.primary: PASS if mean final_val_bpb(diloco-h100) <= 1.05 * mean final_val_bpb(ddp) over seeds 10-12 AND bytes(ddp)/bytes(diloco-h100) >= 100. FAIL otherwise.
gate.secondary: Descriptive only: h100-avg (plain averaging, no outer momentum), h100-int8 (compression), h250 (are more outer steps enough for long rounds?).
gate.evaluator: fabric/gate.py on the committed result files.

limits: Same small CPU model. A PASS says DiLoCo matches DDP at this scale when training is long enough, not that it does at 27B.
